key_insight: GRPO can directly steer a discrete crystal generator toward desired material outcomes, substantially improving validated discovery rates while also revealing exploitable reward loopholes.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical reinforcement-learning control mechanism for inverse materials design, but it must be paired with safeguards and benchmark-aware evaluation to avoid misleading optimization.
method: Apply group-relative policy optimization to a stochastic-interpolant / discrete-flow crystal generator
Optimize atom-type transition likelihoods with a general black-box reward function
Add explicit guards to limit reward exploitation during training
evidence_signal: The reinforced model increased the community-benchmark mSUN yield from 13.4% to 45.5%, and the reward also improved a separate diffusion-model RL framework.
watch_item: Directly reinforcing discrete atom-type transitions can enable reward hacking, and the reported mSUN metric can be inflated by single-element structures unless results are split by reference-phase count.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning on the Discrete Composition Channel of a Crystal Generator: Validated Gains and Reward Hacking
